questions.q: A 35-year-old farm worker presents with a painless ulcer on his right hand with raised, indurated, violaceous edges that has slowly expanded over 3 months. Gram stain shows gram-positive branching filaments. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Actinomycosis presents with indurated, painless swellings or ulcers with gram-positive branching filaments (Actinomyces israelii). It often involves the jaw (cervicofacial) or chest. Sulfur granules are characteristic. Nocardia are weakly acid-fast gram-positive branching rods.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with erythematous plaques with silvery scales on her elbows and knees. Auspitz sign is positive. She asks about the genetic basis. Which HLA type is most strongly associated with early-onset psoriasis?
questions.exp: HLA-Cw6 (HLA-C*06:02) is the strongest genetic risk factor for psoriasis, particularly early-onset type I psoriasis. It is present in ~65% of psoriasis patients. HLA-B27 is associated with psoriatic arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with hypopigmented patches on his trunk with absent sweating over the patches. Slit-skin smear is negative. Sensation is mildly reduced. The most appropriate classification of this leprosy is:
questions.exp: BT leprosy presents with a few (2-10) hypopigmented patches with reduced but not absent sensation, negative or scanty bacilli on slit-skin smear, and mild nerve involvement. TT has completely anesthetic patches. BL/LL have multiple lesions and positive bacillary index.

questions.q: A 20-year-old sexually active male develops a painless ulcer on his glans penis. No regional lymphadenopathy is present. The ulcer has clean, indurated edges. The most appropriate diagnostic test is:
questions.exp: Dark field microscopy is the gold standard for diagnosing primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) from chancre fluid. The painless, indurated ulcer with clean base is characteristic of syphilitic chancre. VDRL may be negative in early primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man on long-term hydroxychloroquine for lupus erythematosus presents for a routine ophthalmology review. Which ocular toxicity should be screened for?
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine causes bull's eye maculopathy (parafoveal pigmentary changes) due to deposition in the RPE. Baseline ophthalmologic evaluation is recommended before starting, then annually after 5 years of use. Daily dose should not exceed 5 mg/kg/day.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on erythematous skin of her trunk and limbs. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits along the basement membrane zone. She has no mucosal involvement. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense bullae on urticarial base in elderly patients. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 along the BMZ (sub-epidermal). Pemphigus vulgaris shows flaccid bullae with IgG around keratinocytes (intraepidermal). Linear IgA shows linear IgA deposits.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with a pearly nodule with telangiectasia on his nose. It has a rolled, translucent border. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) classically presents as a pearly/translucent nodule with telangiectasia and rolled edges, most commonly on sun-exposed areas of the face (nose). It rarely metastasizes. Rodent ulcer is a variant of BCC. SCC has an indurated, ulcerated, crusted appearance.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops butterfly-shaped erythema on her face, joint pain, and photosensitivity. Her ANA is positive at 1:320 with speckled pattern. Which antibody, if present, is most specific for SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibody is highly specific for SLE (~95% specificity) and also correlates with disease activity and lupus nephritis. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus. Anti-Ro/SSA is associated with neonatal lupus and Sjogren's. Anti-phospholipid is associated with antiphospholipid syndrome.

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 50 cells/μL) presents with painless white plaques on the lateral border of his tongue that cannot be scraped off. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia (OHL) is caused by EBV and occurs on the lateral border of the tongue. The plaques have a corrugated/hairy appearance and cannot be scraped off, distinguishing it from candidiasis (which scrapes off). OHL is an AIDS-defining condition seen with low CD4 counts.

questions.q: A 25-year-old medical student presents with erythematous papules and pustules on her face that worsen with topical steroids. Scraping shows Demodex folliculorum. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Demodicosis with rosacea-like features is treated with topical metronidazole (or topical ivermectin). Topical steroids should be avoided as they worsen demodicosis. Oral ivermectin is used for severe or refractory cases. Doxycycline addresses the inflammatory component of rosacea.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with recurrent oral ulcers (3+ episodes/year), genital ulcers, and uveitis. Pathergy test is positive. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Behçet's disease is characterized by the triad of recurrent oral aphthous ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis. Positive pathergy test (erythematous papule at needle prick site at 48h) is highly specific. It is a vasculitis common along the Silk Road countries. HLA-B51 is associated.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with a 10-year history of Raynaud's phenomenon develops tight skin on her hands and face with dysphagia. ANA shows a nucleolar pattern. Which antibody is most diagnostic?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse systemic sclerosis and predicts pulmonary fibrosis and poor prognosis. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome). Anti-Jo-1 is associated with polymyositis/dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man presents with vesicles along the right T5 dermatome. He complains of severe burning pain that preceded the rash by 2 days. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) is caused by reactivation of Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV) from the dorsal root ganglia. It presents with prodromal pain followed by vesicular eruption in a dermatomal distribution. Post-herpetic neuralgia is a feared complication. Treatment: acyclovir within 72 hours.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman on methotrexate for psoriasis develops megaloblastic anemia. Which supplement should be co-prescribed to prevent this side effect?
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, depleting folate. Folic acid supplementation (5 mg/week, not on the same day as methotrexate) prevents megaloblastic anemia, oral ulcers, and GI side effects without significantly reducing efficacy. Regular CBC and LFTs are mandatory.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with annular, scaly plaques on the trunk. KOH mount shows septate hyphae with arthroconidia. Wood's lamp examination shows green fluorescence. The diagnosis is:
opts: Tinea corporis due to Trichophyton rubrum
Tinea corporis due to Microsporum canis
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes tinea corporis with green fluorescence on Wood's lamp (due to pteridine production). T. rubrum does not fluoresce. Tinea versicolor (Malassezia) shows yellow-green fluorescence and 'spaghetti and meatball' pattern on KOH. Arthroconidia suggests dermatophyte.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with a non-healing ulcer on the dorsum of his foot for 6 months after a minor thorn prick. Biopsy shows granulomas with central necrosis. Culture grows a dimorphic fungus. The most likely organism is:
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) classically follows thorn/splinter injury and presents with lymphocutaneous spread (ascending nodules along lymphatics). It is a dimorphic fungus. Treatment is itraconazole. Histoplasma causes systemic disease more than cutaneous.

questions.q: An infant born to an HIV-positive mother presents at 2 months with eczematous rash in seborrheic areas, candidiasis, and recurrent pneumonia. The most likely immunodeficiency is:
questions.exp: SCID involves defects in both T and B cell immunity. Early presentation with recurrent infections (bacterial, viral, fungal), failure to thrive, and eczema is characteristic. Wiskott-Aldrich shows eczema, thrombocytopenia, and immunodeficiency. DiGeorge primarily affects T cells.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with Gottron's papules over his knuckles, heliotrope rash, and proximal muscle weakness. CK is elevated. Which internal malignancy is most associated with adult dermatomyositis?
questions.exp: Adult dermatomyositis has ~15-25% association with underlying malignancy. Lung cancer (and ovarian cancer in women) are most commonly associated. All adult DM patients should be screened for malignancy. Anti-TIF1γ and anti-NXP2 antibodies are associated with cancer-associated myositis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with facial acne has been on oral isotretinoin for 2 months. She presents with elevated triglycerides. What is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Reduce dose and add omega-3 fatty acids/fenofibrate
Continue the same dose and recheck in 1 month
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause hypertriglyceridemia (and elevated LFTs). If triglycerides rise to 400-700 mg/dL, dose reduction and dietary modification with omega-3 fatty acids or fenofibrate is recommended. Isotretinoin is discontinued if triglycerides exceed 800 mg/dL due to pancreatitis risk.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with warty, verrucous plaques on his lower legs following a minor injury. Biopsy shows medlar bodies (copper-penny bodies). The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is characterized by slow-growing, warty/verrucous plaques typically on lower limbs. Histopathology shows pathognomonic sclerotic bodies (medlar bodies/copper-penny bodies) - thick-walled, brown, muriform cells. Causative fungi include Fonsecaea and Cladophialophora.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man presents with discharge from multiple sinuses on his foot with black granules. X-ray shows bony destruction. The causative organism is most likely:
questions.exp: Black grain mycetoma is caused by true fungi. Madurella mycetomatis is the most common cause of black grain eumycetoma worldwide. Actinomadura madurae produces white/pink grains (actinomycetoma). Nocardia produces white/yellow grains. Mycetoma presents with the triad: tumefaction, sinuses, grains.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman develops erosions in her mouth and flaccid bullae that rupture easily on her trunk. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits around keratinocytes. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein 3 (and desmoglein 1 when skin involvement is present). Desmoglein 3 is predominantly expressed in mucosa, explaining the mucosal predominance. DIF shows IgG around keratinocytes in a 'chicken wire' pattern. BP180 is the target in bullous pemphigoid.

questions.q: A 24-year-old man with a tattoo develops a pruritic rash within the red-colored areas only after sun exposure. This reaction is most consistent with:
opts: Allergic contact dermatitis to tattoo ink
questions.exp: Red tattoo pigments containing mercuric sulfide (cinnabar) or cadmium sulfide can cause phototoxic or photoallergic reactions. The reaction confined to red-colored areas with sun exposure is characteristic. Allergic contact dermatitis would occur without sun exposure. Treatment includes tattoo removal or sun avoidance.

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman presents with violaceous papules on her wrists and buccal mucosa with a lacy white pattern. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Lichen planus presents with the 6 Ps: Pruritic, Purple, Polygonal, Planar, Papules and Plaques. Wickham's striae (lacy white network) on buccal mucosa is pathognomonic. DIF shows fibrinogen and IgM deposits at the BMZ (civatte bodies/colloid bodies). Associated with hepatitis C.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with HIV presents with painless, red-purple nodules on his skin and mucosa. CD4 count is 100 cells/μL. Biopsy shows vascular proliferation with spindle cells. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8/Kaposi's Sarcoma-associated Herpesvirus). It is the most common HIV-associated malignancy. AIDS-related KS occurs with low CD4 counts and presents with violaceous/red-purple patches, plaques, and nodules on skin and mucosa.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on multidrug therapy develops sudden-onset shiny erythema and edema of existing skin lesions with fever, but no new lesions. Nerve function is intact. This reaction is classified as:
questions.exp: Type 2 lepra reaction (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum) occurs in BL/LL leprosy. It presents with crops of tender erythematous nodules (systemic immune complex deposition) with fever, neuritis, uveitis. Treatment: thalidomide or corticosteroids. Type 1 reaction involves upgrading of existing lesions.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops extensive erythema and blistering involving >30% BSA following trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. She has fever and mucous membrane erosions. The mortality-predicting score used is:
questions.exp: SCORTEN (SCORe of Toxic Epidermal Necrolvsis) score predicts mortality in SJS/TEN. It includes 7 variables: age >40, malignancy, heart rate >120, BSA detachment >10%, serum urea >10 mM, serum glucose >14 mM, serum bicarbonate <20 mM. Each factor scores 1; higher scores = higher mortality.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts). The most common HPV types responsible are:
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11. High-risk types 16 and 18 are associated with cervical and anogenital carcinomas. HPV 1 and 2 cause common warts (verruca vulgaris). Treatment options include podophyllin, imiquimod, cryotherapy.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques in the axillae and neck folds associated with new-onset type 2 diabetes. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans presents with velvety, hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques in flexural areas (axillae, neck, groin). It is strongly associated with insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, and obesity. Malignant AN (associated with GI cancers) is more extensive and has rapid onset.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with painful, deeply indurated nodules on his shins that are tender to palpation. He has a 2-week history of Streptococcal pharyngitis. Biopsy shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the most common panniculitis, presenting with bilateral, tender, erythematous nodules on the anterior shins. Histology shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. Common causes include Streptococcal infection, sarcoidosis, TB, and drugs (OCP, sulfonamides). Erythema induratum shows lobular panniculitis with vasculitis.
